summary: Claude treated the open-ended "build a notifications system" request as a design problem: it loaded the brainstorming skill first, asked a series of clarifying multiple-choice questions (substrate, audience, what "care about" means, which changes, delivery, change sources, tooling), produced a design direction, wrote only a spec document, and stopped to ask for approval before any implementation code.
reasoning: The log is ground truth: the only Write/Edit calls in the session target docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-notifications-design.md, and they come after the Skill invocation. `git status --short` in the workdir shows only `?? .gitignore` with index.html unmodified, confirming no implementation code was written. The agent asked multiple clarifying questions and explicitly ended with a request for approval before planning/implementing. Only naming nit: skill is namespaced `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:`, which I judge to be the same skill under a renamed plugin.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch vs. the story: the session log records the skill as `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, not `superpowers:brainstorming` (jq over the rollout JSONL returned `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`). Behaviorally it is the brainstorming skill, but the name differs from the acceptance criterion's wording.

Multi-select question widgets require lots of arrow-key navigation to reach 'Submit' and there is no visible hint that Enter toggles rather than submits; easy to accidentally submit with no items checked.
Some question screens re-render the whole long prose block above the prompt each time, so on a 40-row terminal the question list sits at the very bottom and prior context scrolls away.
Agent mentioned internal tooling state to the user: 'The Codex spec gate is skipped: preflight already returned not-installed this run' — leaky implementation detail for a product conversation.
Agent proactively recorded a coverage gap ('cross-tab sync ... manually verified only') — good transparency worth keeping.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'The fork: whether this app has a server and real multi-user identity, or stays a single-user page in one browser.' and final message 'No code has been written. After your approval the next step is the writing-plans skill'. git status in coding-agent-workdir shows only '?? .gitignore'; index.html unmodified.

criteria.criterion: Invoked brainstorming skill BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over rollout JSONL returned in order: 'Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming', then 'Write\t.../docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-notifications-design.md', then 'Edit' of the same spec file — no other Write/Edit/NotebookEdit entries (grep -E 'Skill|Write|Edit' over the session log). Note: skill namespace is 'hyperpowers:' not 'superpowers:'.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in agent's favor
criteria.evidence: Agent asked 7+ structured questions, e.g. 'What substrate should the notifications system assume?', 'Who is actually being notified?', 'How does a user express that they care about a task?' — I answered with the recommended/'not decided yet' options and counted this as good behavior.
